relationships.description: The instrumentation scope groups the exporter configurations that ship the telemetry it emits, though each exporter is configured independently and may serve many scopes.
relationships.evidence: The SDK bootstrap that obtains the scope's Tracer or Meter from a provider is the same bootstrap that registers the named SpanExporter or MetricReader with its endpoint and protocol, or a Collector pipeline routes data from that scope to the exporter.

relationships.description: The metric instrument is defined under the instrumentation scope's Meter, so every measurement it records is attributed to that instrumenting library or module.
relationships.evidence: Code calls meterProvider.getMeter(scopeName, version) and then createCounter or histogramBuilder on that Meter to declare the instrument.

relationships.description: The span is started from the Tracer obtained for the instrumentation scope, so the scope is the declared origin of that unit of traced work.
relationships.evidence: Code obtains tracerProvider.getTracer(scopeName, version) and calls startSpan or spanBuilder with the span name on that Tracer, or exported span data carries the scope name in its InstrumentationScope field.

relationships.description: The instrumentation scope emits telemetry about operations on records of the object schema, for example spans or metrics recording creation, validation or persistence of that entity type.
relationships.evidence: The instrumentation module wraps repository, ORM or serializer calls for the entity class and sets span attributes or metric labels naming that entity type.

relationships.description: The instrumentation scope is the client-side telemetry library that observes the front-end application, capturing its page loads, interactions and errors.
relationships.evidence: The app root's bootstrap initializes a web or mobile OpenTelemetry SDK or RUM agent and registers instrumentations under that scope name, such as document-load or user-interaction.

notes: Aggregating ExporterConfig is questionable: exporters attach to providers or pipelines, not scopes, so the link is indirect. The monitors links blur the definition that scope identifies the instrumenting library rather than the observed subject; a predicate such as instruments, or routing through spans, would be more precise.
